correctness.rationale: For each fixed vertex, the reciprocal-neighbor condition is a rectangle of exact area \(XY\); independent third vertices give a binomial mixture with product-uniform density \(-\log t\), and beta differentiation gives \((H_n-H_k)/n\). For two tagged reciprocal isolates, the exact probability is \(\mathbb E[\mathbf 1_{E_{12}^{\mathrm c}}q^{n-2}]\) with \(q=1-z_1-z_2+\min(x_1,x_2)\min(y_1,y_2)\). Direct mutual edges contribute \(o(n^{-2})\). After \(t_i=n x_i y_i\) and \(u_i=-\log x_i\), the logarithmic u-overlap gives an extra \(2\log n\) of covariance: the limiting kernel expectation at aspect-ratio separation delta is \(e^{-|\delta|}\), integrable to two; explicit exponential domination and an \(O((\log n)^2/n)\) remainder justify the exchange of limit and integral. The diagonal contribution is \(H_n+o(1)\), yielding variance \(3\log n+o(\log n)\) and a Chebyshev law of large numbers. The included actual checker separately returned 4246 exact and seeded assertions; simulation is not used to establish the limit.

value.rationale: Reciprocal confirmation is a standard natural network statistic distinct from both directed degree and weak undirected adjacency. The theorem gives an interpretable complete expected reciprocal-degree spectrum and a nontrivial sharp variance inflation factor for its most important rare class (mutual-edge isolates). This requires analysis of dependence through overlapping two-dimensional rectangles and logarithmic aspect ratios; it is not just a textbook binomial mixture identity. It supports uncertainty calculations in mutual-confirmation networks even where ordinary directed isolation nearly disappears. The work makes no unsupported CLT or applications claim.
